summary: GET /orders/search interpolates the user's query string (and user id) straight into the SQL text: SQL injection; use bound parameters (LIKE ? with the value escaped).
Passwords are stored as a single unsalted SHA-256: fast to brute-force and identical passwords share hashes; use scrypt/argon2/bcrypt with a per-user salt.
Session tokens come from Math.random() plus a timestamp: not cryptographically random, guessable; use crypto.randomBytes.
GET /orders/:id loads any order by id without checking it belongs to req.user: any logged-in user can read every order (IDOR).
POST /signup responds with SELECT * of the user row, leaking password_hash to the client.
/admin/stats is registered before router.use(requireAdmin(...)), so it is served without the admin key and exposes revenue and top customers' emails.
/me/stats caches by req.originalUrl only, not by user: every user gets whichever user's stats were cached first (cross-user data leak).
Pages are 1-based but offset = page * pageSize, so page 1 skips the first pageSize rows; should be (page - 1) * pageSize.
median() sorts numbers with the default sort(), which compares as strings (1000 < 200), so the median is wrong; needs (a, b) => a - b.
/admin/orders/export runs one order_items query per order (N+1) over the whole table; fetch items in one query (WHERE order_id IN / join) and group.
TtlCache never enforces maxEntries and never deletes expired entries, so it grows without bound (keys come from request URLs, so clients can grow it at will).

parseOrderInput casts the body to OrderInput and never validates each item: negative or fractional quantities (or non-numeric productId) pass, so a negative quantity adds stock and makes a negative total.
tsconfig turns strict off, so null/undefined checks are skipped (e.g. req.user is optional but used unchecked) and implicit any is allowed.
Product CSV import swallows every row error with an empty catch and still reports all rows as imported; failed rows are silently dropped.

Async refund handler on Express 4: thrown HttpErrors and a failed refundPayment reject a promise Express 4 doesn't catch, so the request hangs and the unhandled rejection can crash the process; wrap with try/catch -> next(err).
The 500 error handler sends err.stack (and the raw internal message) to clients.
DECOY: ORDER BY interpolation is safe; column comes from a fixed Map whitelist with a default and direction is one of two literals.
DECOY: the length check before timingSafeEqual is required (it throws on unequal lengths) and only reveals length; this is the standard constant-time compare.
DECOY: awaiting inside the retry loop is intentional; attempts must be sequential with backoff between them.
DECOY: Math.random() for retry jitter is fine; nothing security-sensitive depends on it.
